theme: The vine; the unfaithful wife; the two eagles
readingInstruction: Read Ezekiel 15:1-17:24. Three parables: a useless vine, an unfaithful wife, and two eagles with a cedar. Read the second one, in chapter 16, carefully. It is among the most intense chapters in the Bible, and it ends with an everlasting covenant.
settingTheScene: Ezekiel uses a series of images to explain Jerusalem’s history. Chapter 15 compares Israel to the wood of a vine, which is good for nothing but fire. Chapter 16 tells the story of a foundling girl who was rescued by God, adorned, married, and then unfaithful. Chapter 17 uses two eagles and a cedar shoot to describe Zedekiah’s rebellion against Babylon. They explain why Jerusalem is falling and prepare for the promise of restoration.
observation: “How does the wood of the vine surpass any wood, the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?” (15:2).
“On the day you were born your navel cord was not cut… No eye pitied you… but you were cast out on the open field” (16:4-5).
“I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood, and I said to you in your blood, Live!” (16:6).
“I spread the corner of my garment over you and covered your nakedness; I made my vow to you and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord GOD, and you became mine” (16:8).
“But you trusted in your beauty and played the whore because of your renown” (16:15).
“Yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant” (16:60).
“I will take a sprig from the lofty top of the cedar and will plant it” (17:22).
“And all the trees of the field shall know that I am the LORD; I bring low the high tree, and make high the low tree” (17:24).
interpretation:
The vine in chapter 15 is a short parable with a clear point. A vine is valuable for its fruit. Its wood is useless for building. A vine that does not bear fruit is only for fire. Jerusalem’s status as God’s vine does not protect her. If she does not bear fruit, she is fuel. The people had grown proud of their position. Ezekiel says that position without fruit is worthless.

The story of chapter 16 is a long and unsettling picture. A baby is abandoned in a field, unwashed, uncut, with no one to pity her. God passes by and says, “Live!” He raises her, and when she is grown, he enters into a covenant with her, clothes her in fine linen and jewelry, and makes her queen. This is the history of Israel from Abraham, a rescued foundling. She is adopted and adorned. Then she trusts in her beauty and uses her gifts to play the prostitute with every passerby: Egypt, Assyria, Babylon. She even sacrifices her children. She is worse than Sodom.

The chapter is hard to read, and it is meant to be. It shows the ugliness of idolatry from God’s point of view: not just rule-breaking but betrayal of love. Everything Israel had was a gift, and she used it against the giver.

Yet the end of the chapter is astonishing. “Yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant.” God will make atonement for her. “That you may remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth again because of your shame, when I atone for you for all that you have done.” Grace is the final word.

Chapter 17 ends with another promise: God himself will take a sprig from the top of the cedar and plant it on a high mountain, where it becomes a noble cedar. It is a messianic promise, the Davidic king who will shelter all birds.
connection: Jesus said, “I am the true vine” (John 15:1-6) and warned that branches that bear no fruit are thrown into the fire. Ephesians 5:25-27 says Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her to present her to himself in splendor. Romans 5:8 says that God showed his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. Mark 4:30-32 describes the kingdom as a mustard seed that becomes a tree where birds find shelter. Hebrews 13:20 speaks of the blood of the eternal covenant.
application:
Remember where you came from: you were like the abandoned baby in the field, and God said “Live!”

Think about the gifts God has given you. Are you using them for him?

Receive the promise of an everlasting covenant, and rest in the atonement made for you.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for finding you cast out, and telling you to live.
Thank him for covering you and entering into covenant.
Confess where you have been unfaithful.
